transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I just can’t shake this feeling that work isn’t safe anymore. And I keep feeling like something in me is damaged now, like the person who was competent enough to get promoted… isn’t really there anymore.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially since this issue at work started?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve been upset and kind of worn down by all of it, but I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless. I haven’t really been paying attention to whether I’m enjoying things less. Right now it just feels like work has been taking up all the space in my head.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you used to care about, even before the problems at work started taking up so much of your mind?

Before the work stuff got really bad, I don’t think so. I mean, I had normal stressful days, but I don’t remember feeling consistently down or like I’d stopped caring about things. It’s more that since all this started, it’s been hard to tell what I feel outside of it.
Before any of this work stress started, did you notice yourself losing interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
No, I don’t think so. Before the work stress started, I was still interested in the things I usually liked. I wasn’t noticing any real loss of pleasure or anything like that.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious or on edge about your work situation?

Yes. I feel on edge a lot. Like on the train, or even in meetings, I’m automatically checking where the exits are, noticing who’s standing too close to me. At lunch with my team I’m not really relaxed—I’m half listening for noises in the hallway instead of being fully there.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or on edge even when you're not at work or thinking about work?

Yes. It’s not only at work. Like on the train, I’ll catch myself checking where the exits are or watching who’s standing too close. Even at lunch or in meetings, I’m kind of listening for noises in the hallway instead of being fully in the conversation. It’s hard to switch off.
Have you been having intrusive, distressing memories or flashbacks about a specific event at work that’s been bothering you?

Yes. Certain things set it off really suddenly—like a badge scanner beeping, or heavy footsteps in the hallway, or even a late-night deployment alert. It’s like I’m back in that office for a second. My chest gets tight, and I see the guard on the floor in my mind, even if I’m trying to focus on something else.
Can you tell me about the event in the office that you keep remembering when you hear those sounds or get those feelings?

It was in the office, and there was this moment where the guard was on the floor. That’s the part that keeps coming back. I don’t even have to be thinking about it—if I hear a badge scanner beep, or heavy footsteps in the hall, or one of those late-night deployment alerts, it just hits me. For a second it feels like I’m right back there, and my chest gets tight. That image cuts through whatever I’m doing.
Can you tell me if the moment with the guard on the floor involved actual or threatened serious harm or death, and whether you felt intense fear, helplessness, or horror at the time?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I know it felt really serious in the moment, and I remember being scared and kind of frozen. But I don’t know exactly what the level of danger was, or how to describe it beyond that.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, like feeling on edge, having intrusive memories, and being startled by certain sounds?
It’s been going on since the break-in during that overnight deployment. So… about two years and four months now.
